title: Learning design to support student-AI collaboration: perspectives of leading teachers for AI in education
extended_summary:
This paper examines how K-12 education should be designed when artificial intelligence is introduced as a collaborative learning agent rather than only as a tool. The authors focus on student-AI collaboration (SAC) and ask what curriculum, interaction supports, learning environments, and developmental stages are needed for students to work productively with AI in learning.

The study uses a qualitative design based on in-depth semi-structured interviews with 10 Korean leading teachers in AI in education, including both primary and secondary school teachers. Participants were drawn from schools involved in Korea’s software education and AI pilot initiatives, and interviews explored teachers’ views on learning goals, content, assessment, student-AI interaction, and environmental supports for SAC.

Findings suggest that SAC should aim at capacity building, subject-matter understanding, interdisciplinary and authentic tasks, creative work, process-oriented and collaboration-based assessment, and supports such as AI principles, data literacy, error analysis, AI ethics, and intuitive interfaces. Teachers also emphasized flexible spaces, robust digital infrastructure, strong institutional policy, and a collaborative, safe-to-fail culture. They expected SAC to evolve through three stages: learn about AI, learn from AI, and learn together. The paper concludes with a conceptual and design-oriented framework for supporting student-AI collaboration in K-12 schools.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: A generic AI/GenAI tutoring or collaborative learning agent that can provide instructional scaffolding, personalized feedback, content support, and adaptive interaction in learning tasks.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper is a qualitative study of K-12 teachers’ perspectives on designing student-AI collaboration, including how AI should support learning goals, interaction, assessment, and environment. It does not evaluate a specific commercial product.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a qualitative interview study focused on teachers’ perspectives and a conceptual student-AI collaboration model, not an empirical evaluation of a specific AI tool. No causal design, effect estimates, or outcome measures are reported.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper has clear conceptual relevance for K-12 AI design and literacy-adjacent learning practices, but it reports no measured impact on student outcomes. As a result, impact on literacy outcomes is theoretical and unquantified.
